Additional comments:
questions.answer: I can highly recommend taking the initiative and sent e-mails to group leaders if you are truly interested in the project.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my traineeship host

questions.question: How easy was it to find housing? *
questions.answer: Getting housing through the institution was very convenient, but it was rather last minute. Hence, I tried to organize something myself and that was very difficult (for Paris, short-term rental that is not extremely expensive).

questions.question: Additional comments:
How relevant did you find your traineeship for your future employment prospects? *
questions.answer: Very useful! I learned technical skills, generated data that has the potential to be incorporated in a publication, and I also increased my network. Last but not least, I got a taste of how a potential career could look like.

questions.question: How relevant did you find your traineeship for your academic programme at UCPH *
questions.answer: Also very useful! The Human Biology program doesn't give much opportunity for practical work in the first year, so it is very useful to gain more experience, especially it is complementary to the work I will do during my master thesis.

questions.question: Additional comments
How well did the academic level at UCPH coincide with the tasks completed during your traineeship? *
questions.answer: I mostly relied on the practical training/skills I required during from my Bachelors programs (Germany). But for theoretical aspects, where I applied by knowledge from my KU program, the academic level of the education of KU matched well with the requirements.

questions.question: Please elaborate *
questions.answer: My master program from KU (Human biology) allowed my to see the broader theoretical context, especially the pharmacological and pathophysiological aspects of the project.

questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
In general, costs of living are lower in Paris than Copenhagen.
However, housing costs (if not with student housing, e.g. Cité universitaire de Paris, CUIP) are similar to CPH, but often for less space/quality.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your traineeship destination (city/region)? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Paris is a big city with many things to do! Check out events with your institution, the CIUP (student campus) etc.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available at your traineeship destination (organization/city/region)? *
questions.answer: Basically every thing! The institute had sports and language courses, and social events. Same for the student campus I was living at, as well as for the city.

questions.question: Which non-academic activities would you recommend to future trainees visiting the same destination (organization/city/region)? Why? *
questions.answer: Institut Pasteur offers sports events, and also a Friday Bar (aka Stapa) for young scientists. Also, check out events at CIUP!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting trainees see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Once a months the museums in Paris are for free! Check out the dates in advances, as tickets are sold out fast!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your trainee host? *
questions.answer: Easy, as Institut Pasteur is very international. Hence, people are very understanding if you struggle with language barriers etc. and are aware of potential cultural differences etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of the destination (city/country)? *
questions.answer: Knowing French is a big advantage in day to day life, it will make your life much easier. Nevertheless, it is definitely possible to get around the city with English. Adjusting to the local culture is also absolutely doable, as long as you are open to it. But be prepared for locals being very direct ;)

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with locals? *
questions.answer:
Learn as much French as you can in advance!
People usually speak English (especially younger people) but are often shy about it and hence reluctant to use it. You will be able to get around without it, but in order to make local friends I would advise to speak French at a conversational level (but don't worry if you don't, there is always a big international community you can turn to)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: French people, and especially Parisians, tend to complain a lot and come of as pretty negative (yes, the cliches are true). Try to see the fun side of it, it can be entertaining to tap into your inner drama queen (or king).

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The culture around food is huge! Don't miss out on it! Also, people are interactive and it is very easy to start a conversation with strangers.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going on a traineeship to the same city/region? *
questions.answer:
1. Learn French
2. Go out and enjoy the food at cafes or bars and go to as many museums and galleries as you can
3. Talk to strangers! it's fun ;-)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future traineeship students? *
questions.answer: See last question ("Any other comments?")

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your traineeship experience? *
questions.answer:
Seeing that over the course of 2 months I could manage to built a circle of friends, and gain enough experience at the trainee-ship to be able to work independently and to produce something useful. At the end, I presented my work and got positive feedback on it, which was indeed very rewarding.
Leaving my new friends behind here is sad, but it is also great to know, that it is possible to make new friends wherever you are, and it gives you a good excuse to travel in order to see them again!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the traineeship? *
questions.answer: Overcoming the first weekends, as I didn't know to many people so it felt a bit lonely. But it is part of the process and you will make more and more friends!

questions.question: Is there anything UCPH could have done different (before/during/after) in regard to the traineeship experience? *
questions.answer:
Yes!!! I was quite disappointed by the lack of help I received for the Erasmus grand application. I had a few of specific questions on requirements (that are not specified on KUnet), which the student guidance could not answer, and the outgoing mobility e-mail was very, very slow in replying. I almost couldn't go because of this and it took a lot of (unnecessary) work to make it happen. A physical international office would have made a huge difference!
Also, the regulation, that KU students are only allowed to obtain more than ~3.000 DKK per month from the institution (at least for Human Biologists) was not helpful, as it is mandatory in France to pay interns (~ 4.000 DKK/month). And for international/ EU students, who cannot receive SU, this is absolutely vital.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Your internship must be EXACTLY 60 days long! this way you are eligible to obtain an Erasmus trainee-ship grant (min. 60 days), but are not obliged to get payed by French law (up to 60 days).

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
